name: Mean Dependency Depth (MDD)
description: Measures the structural complexity of sentences by analyzing the average 'distance' (depth) between a sentence's root verb and its dependent words in a grammatical parse tree. AI models generally generate sentences with shallower, simpler dependency structures to minimize syntax errors, whereas humans naturally construct sentences with highly variable, deeper nesting.
mechanism: This method utilizes a Natural Language Processing (NLP) dependency parser to map the grammatical structure of every sentence in the text. It identifies the 'root' of the sentence (usually the main verb) and builds a syntactic tree detailing how subjects, objects, and modifiers depend on each other. The 'Dependency Depth' is the number of grammatical links between the root and the most distant dependent word. The algorithm calculates the Mean Dependency Depth (MDD) across all sentences. Because LLMs operate via autoregressive next-token prediction, keeping track of deeply nested, long-distance grammatical dependencies (e.g., a subject separated from its verb by three relative clauses) requires significant 'attention' computation and risks breaking grammar. Consequently, model alignment heavily favors generating text with flat, straightforward syntactic trees (low MDD). Human writers, especially in formal or academic settings, organically write with deeper syntactic embedding, holding complex structures in their working memory. If a long, supposedly sophisticated text exhibits an unnaturally shallow Mean Dependency Depth bordering on simplistic syntax, it is strongly flagged as machine-generated.
useCase: Essential for evaluating long-form argumentative essays, literature, and technical papers to determine if the grammatical complexity matches the expected intellectual depth of human writing.
strengths:
• Highly resistant to basic prompt engineering; asking an AI to 'write more complexly' usually results in the model adding more adjectives or rare vocabulary, rather than fundamentally deepening its internal syntactic parsing tree.
• Analyzes deep structural grammar rather than surface-level vocabulary, making it completely immune to synonym-swapping bots.
• Language-independent, provided an accurate dependency parser exists for the target language.
limitations:
• Extremely high computational cost, as generating a full dependency parse tree for every sentence is resource-intensive.
• Short texts (under 150 words) may not offer enough sentences to establish a statistically significant MDD baseline.
• Texts inherently meant to be simple (e.g., children's books, bulleted instructions, simple emails) will naturally have low MDD, causing potential false positives.
parameters:
Analysis: NLP Dependency Tree Parsing per Sentence
Metric: Average Path Length from Root to Terminal Nodes
Output: 0-100 Syntactic Flatness (Algorithmic Simplicity) Score
accuracy: High — 78-86% accuracy on complex or academic text. It exposes the AI's core architectural preference for structural safety and predictable grammar.
